title: The product of a singleton multiset is its element
statement: The product of the multiset containing a single copy of a is a. The fold runs over [0, a+1) and every factor strictly below a has multiplicity 0, so it must collapse to 1 -- including the factor at 0, where a fold that forgot the multiplicity would give 0.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Multiset.prod_singleton : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Multiset.prod (AxNat.Multiset.singleton x0)) x0)

evidence.supports: Nat.Multiset.prod_singleton is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Multiset.prod_singleton 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE '^Nat\.Multiset\.prod_singleton.1.\(\(x0 : AxNat\) -> Eq\.\{1\} AxNat \(AxNat\.Multiset\.prod \(AxNat\.Multiset\.singleton x0\)\) x0\)$')" = 1

notes: Not free, and the two reasons are worth separating. The fold runs over `[0, a+1)` so every factor strictly below `a` must collapse, which is `Nat.prodRange_eq_one_of_below` plus `count_singleton_of_ne`; and the top factor `pow a 1` reduces only as far as `mul 1 a`, because `Nat.mul` recurses on its RIGHT argument and that term is STUCK for symbolic `a` -- the last step is `Nat.one_mul`, not reduction. It says nothing about `prod` of a multiset built any other way.
